title: Colours
summary: Name the basic colours and describe things with them, using the right masculine or feminine form.
intro: Colours are adjectives, so they come after the noun and agree with it. The basic colours have two shapes: أَحْمَر (red, masculine) and حَمْرَاء (red, feminine). So it is قَلَم أَحْمَر (a red pen) but سَيَّارَة حَمْرَاء (a red car). Ask about a colour with مَا لَوْنُ …؟ (what is the colour of …?).
objectives: Use the masculine and the feminine form of a colour
Describe the flags of Egypt, Lebanon and Jordan

realLife.title: Flags on the wall
realLife.story: At the end of the week the classroom wall is covered in flags. Mr Karim asks each student to describe a flag in Arabic, and the lesson ends with a quick colour game.

sentences.en: What colour is your car? (to a man)

mistakes.why: sayyāra is feminine, so 'red' is the feminine ḥamrāʾ, not aḥmar.

sentences.en: I have a blue pen and a black bag.
sentences.literal: at me (are) a pen blue and a bag black

sentences.en: The flag of Egypt is red, white and black.
sentences.literal: (the) flag (of) Egypt (is) red and white and black

sentences.en: My house in Cairo is white.

mistakes.why: bayt (house) is masculine, so 'white' is abyaḍ, not the feminine bayḍāʾ.

sentences.en: The tree is green, and the sun is yellow.
sentences.literal: the tree (is) green, and the sun (is) yellow

dialogue.title: The flags of our countries
dialogue.culture: Red, white, black and green are often called the Pan-Arab colours. They appear on the flags of many Arab countries, among them Egypt, Jordan, Palestine, Sudan, the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait.

lines.ar: يَا طُلَّاب، الْيَوْم دَرْسُنَا عَنِ الْأَلْوَان. اُنْظُرُوا إِلَى هٰذِهِ الْأَعْلَام!
lines.en: Students, today our lesson is about colours. Look at these flags!

lines.ar: يَا سَامِي، هٰذَا عَلَمُ مِصْر. مَا أَلْوَانُهُ؟
lines.en: Sami, this is the flag of Egypt. What are its colours?

lines.ar: عَلَمُ مِصْر أَحْمَر وَأَبْيَض وَأَسْوَد، وَفِي الْوَسَط نَسْر ذَهَبِيّ.
lines.en: The flag of Egypt is red, white and black, and in the middle there is a golden eagle.

lines.ar: مُمْتَاز! وَأَنْتِ يَا لَيْلَى؟ مَا لَوْنُ عَلَمِ لُبْنَان؟
lines.en: Excellent! And you, Layla? What colour is the flag of Lebanon?

lines.ar: عَلَمُ لُبْنَان أَحْمَر وَأَبْيَض، وَفِي الْوَسَط أَرْزَة خَضْرَاء.
lines.en: The flag of Lebanon is red and white, and in the middle there is a green cedar tree.

lines.ar: الْأَرْزَة جَمِيلَة جِدًّا! وَعَلَمُ أَمْرِيكَا أَحْمَر وَأَبْيَض وَأَزْرَق.
lines.en: The cedar is very beautiful! And the flag of America is red, white and blue.

lines.ar: صَحِيح. وَعَلَمُ الْأُرْدُنّ؟ يَا سَامِي، أَنْتَ تَعْرِفُهُ، فَصَدِيقُكَ يُوسُف مِنْ عَمَّان.
lines.en: Right. And the flag of Jordan? Sami, you know it, because your friend Yusuf is from Amman.

lines.ar: نَعَم! عَلَمُ الْأُرْدُنّ أَسْوَد وَأَبْيَض وَأَخْضَر، وَفِيهِ مُثَلَّث أَحْمَر وَنَجْمَة بَيْضَاء.
lines.en: Yes! The flag of Jordan is black, white and green, and it has a red triangle and a white star.

lines.ar: وَأَنْتَ يَا دَانْيَال، مَا لَوْنُكَ الْمُفَضَّل؟
lines.en: And you, Daniel, what is your favourite colour?

lines.ar: لَوْنِي الْمُفَضَّل الْأَزْرَق، مِثْلُ النِّيل وَالسَّمَاء فِي الْقَاهِرَة.
lines.en: My favourite colour is blue, like the Nile and the sky in Cairo.

lines.ar: وَأَنَا لَوْنِي الْمُفَضَّل الْأَخْضَر. حَقِيبَتِي خَضْرَاء، وَقَلَمِي أَخْضَر أَيْضًا!
lines.en: And my favourite colour is green. My bag is green, and my pen is green too!

lines.ar: وَالْآن لُعْبَة! أَنَا أَقُولُ لَوْنًا، وَأَنْتُمْ تَقُولُونَ شَيْئًا بِهٰذَا اللَّوْن.
lines.en: And now a game! I say a colour, and you say something of that colour.

lines.ar: اللَّوْن الْأَوَّل: أَصْفَر! يَا لَيْلَى، مَا هُوَ الْأَصْفَر؟
lines.en: The first colour is yellow! Layla, what is yellow?
The sun is yellow, and bananas are yellow too!

lines.ar: أَحْسَنْتِ يَا لَيْلَى! وَالْآن أَبْيَض… يَا دَانْيَال؟
lines.en: Well done, Layla! And now white… Daniel?

lines.ar: بَيْتِي فِي الْقَاهِرَة أَبْيَض… وَالْبَيْت الْأَبْيَض فِي وَاشِنْطُن أَيْضًا!
lines.en: My house in Cairo is white… and so is the White House in Washington!

reading.title: Flags in our class
reading.ar: فِي صَفِّنَا طُلَّاب مِنْ مِصْر وَلُبْنَان وَأَمْرِيكَا، وَهُمْ يَعْرِفُونَ أَلْوَانَ الْأَعْلَام. عَلَمُ مِصْر أَحْمَر وَأَبْيَض وَأَسْوَد. عَلَمُ لُبْنَان أَحْمَر وَأَبْيَض، وَفِيهِ أَرْزَة خَضْرَاء. وَعَلَمُ أَمْرِيكَا أَحْمَر وَأَبْيَض وَأَزْرَق.
reading.en: In our class there are students from Egypt, Lebanon and America, and they know the colours of the flags. The flag of Egypt is red, white and black. The flag of Lebanon is red and white, with a green cedar tree. And the flag of America is red, white and blue.

quiz.prompt: What is the feminine of أَبْيَض (white)?
In the dialogue, what is in the middle of the flag of Lebanon?
Which colour word ends in a tapped r?

completion: Fantastic! You can name and use the colours, and Week 2 is complete. Take the week test to open Week 3.
